A 55-year-old male comes to the emergency department with a one-week history of cough with
blood-tinged sputum and dyspnea. He reports fever, chills, and arthralgias. His vital signs show: -
Temperature: 102°F (38.9°C) - Blood pressure: 159/98 mmHg - Pulse: 80/min - Respirations: 14/min -
O2 saturation: 98% on room air Laboratory findings reveal: Hematology: - Hemoglobin: 12 g/dL -
Hematocrit: 36% - Leukocytes: 7,500/mm^3 with normal differential - Platelets: 107,000/mm^3
Chemistry: - Na+: 138 mEq/L - K+: 4.2 mEq/L - Cl-: 101 mEq/L - HCO3-: 24 mEq/L - BUN: 32 mg/dL -
Creatinine: 1.9 mg/dL - Glucose: 99 mg/dL - Ca2+: 10.0 mg/dL - AST: 11 U/L - ALT: 10 U/L Urinalysis:
- Appearance: Amber, cloudy - RBCs: Positive - Protein: Positive CT chest and blood cultures are
negative. What is the most appropriate next step in management? Answer Choices: (A) Prednisone (B)
Echocardiography to evaluate for endocarditis (C) Pulmonary function tests (D) Anti-neutrophil
cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA) levels (E) Azithromycin (F) Sputum acid-fast bacilli (AFB) testing (G)
Bronchoscopy with biopsy (H) Renal biopsy (I) Empiric treatment with ceftriaxone and azithromycin (J)
Type 4 collagen antibody levels
 A. Renal biopsy
B. Sputum acid-fast bacilli (AFB) testing
C. Empiric treatment with ceftriaxone and azithromycin
D. Prednisone
E. Anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA) levels
F. Azithromycin
G. Bronchoscopy with biopsy
H. Echocardiography to evaluate for endocarditis
I. Pulmonary function tests
J. Type 4 collagen antibody levels
